title: Longest Common Subsequence Between Sorted Arrays
summary: Given an array of integer arrays, each sorted in strictly increasing order, find and return an integer array that represents the longest common subsequence shared by all the arrays.
statement: Given an array of integer arrays, each sorted in strictly increasing order, find and return an integer array that represents the longest common subsequence shared by all the arrays. A subsequence is a sequence derived by deleting some elements from the original sequence without altering the order of the remaining elements.
constraints: Each row has 1 through 100 distinct values in strictly increasing order.
Every value is from 1 through 100; return all values present in every row in increasing order.
hints: Strictly increasing rows contain each value at most once, so a global occurrence count equals a row count.
Count every value across all rows and retain exactly those whose count equals the number of rows.
Increment counts per row; scan values one through one hundred in order and emit full-count values.
No row contributes a duplicate, hence count==number of rows is equivalent to membership in every row; the final numeric scan preserves sorted order.
editorial: No row contributes a duplicate, hence count==number of rows is equivalent to membership in every row; the final numeric scan preserves sorted order.

tests.explanation: Only one and four occur in both sorted arrays.
Two, three, and six occur in all three arrays.
